bonus_finding_stale_test_cache_fix.discovered_via: the new TEST_FAILURE live-deterministic-fixture test (section 3), which genuinely overwrites a real test file and re-runs real validation twice against the SAME sandbox -- found flaky under repeated stress-testing (1 failure in ~11 runs before the fix, 0 in 8 runs after)
bonus_finding_stale_test_cache_fix.root_cause: validation.py::check_tests() invoked `python3 -m pytest . -q` with no cache isolation. pytest's assertion-rewrite cache and __pycache__ are keyed by (path, mtime, size) -- a decomposed job's repair cycle can overwrite a test file and re-validate within the same filesystem mtime granularity, risking a STALE compiled assertion running against the CURRENT source text. Observed live: a corrected `assert add(2, 2) == 4` failed with the impossible-looking `assert 4 == 5` -- the displayed source line was current, but the executed (stale, cached) literal was the OLD wrong value.
bonus_finding_stale_test_cache_fix.why_this_matters: this is a real, if narrow, correctness risk in the VALIDATION TRUTH GATE itself (not merely a test-harness quirk) -- exactly the kind of gap this campaign's own VALIDATION_FIRST principle depends on being trustworthy, especially now that TEST_FAILURE repair cycles are a proven, real, live mechanism.
bonus_finding_stale_test_cache_fix.fix: validation.py::check_tests() now clears __pycache__/.pytest_cache under the sandbox (cache-only artifacts, never user source) immediately before every real test run, and passes `-p no:cacheprovider` to pytest itself. Scoped entirely to check_tests() -- the shared _run_allowlisted()/minimal_env() infrastructure used by every other validator and by bridge.py's agent invocation was NOT touched.
